Grey suit, grey face, a lanyard with no name on it. Compliance Officers are the Counting House's hands: former signatories who read their contracts too late. They do not hurry, and they do not stop.

languages.custom: all languages in which a contract has been written

description.value:
Trait

A creature that starts its turn within 10 feet of the officer and has signed any contract recorded in the Grand Ledger (including a QuestRabbit Contractor Agreement) can't take reactions until the start of its next turn.

Trait

The officer ignores difficult terrain, and magical effects can't reduce its speed or cause it to be restrained.

Actions

The officer makes two Stamp attacks.

Actions

Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage plus 7 (2d6) force damage, and the target is marked PROCESSED until the end of its next turn. A processed creature has disadvantage on saving throws against the officer's Citation.

Actions

The officer reads aloud a breach. One creature within 60 feet that can hear it makes a DC 15 Charisma save [[/save cha dc=15]]. On a failure it takes 27 (6d8) psychic damage and is incapacitated until the end of its next turn as it fills out the form. On a success, half damage.

Reactions

When a creature within 30 feet casts a spell, the officer notes the time. The caster must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution save [[/save con dc=15]] or the spell's duration is halved (minimum 1 round).

biography.value: A towering figure of ledger-grey stone with an abacus for a spine. When a Senior Auditor arrives, the numbers are already wrong, and it is here to make them right—whatever that costs you.

description.value:
Trait

The auditor has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

Trait

When the auditor reduces a creature to 0 hit points, that creature's next death saving throw automatically fails.

Trait

If the auditor takes damage from a single source, it can immediately record the amount. The next time it hits with Assessment, the target takes extra force damage equal to the recorded amount (maximum 30).

Actions

The auditor makes two Assessment attacks and uses Freeze Assets if available.

Actions

Melee Weapon Attack: +12 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 25 (4d8 + 7) bludgeoning damage plus 14 (4d6) force damage.

Actions

Every creature of the auditor's choice within 30 feet makes a DC 19 Wisdom save [[/save wis dc=19]]. On a failure, a creature is restrained by glowing grey figures until the end of its next turn, and any magic items it is attuned to stop functioning for 1 minute. On a success, it is only unable to use attuned items until the end of its next turn.

items.name: The auditor can take 2 legendary actions, choosing from the options below

description.value:
Legendary Actions

Only one option can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn. The auditor regains spent legendary actions at the start of its turn.

448a58d6295c22e2.name: The auditor can take 2 legendary actions, choosing from the options below

description.value:
Legendary Actions

The auditor moves up to its speed without provoking opportunity attacks.

Legendary Actions

The auditor chooses a creature it can see that regained hit points since the auditor's last turn. The creature loses hit points equal to half the amount regained.

biography.value: Crown & Cleaver's Vice President of Hostile Acquisitions: immaculate suits, never the same pen twice, a crimson suit, a smile that has closed more deals than most armies. Veronique wants the chair above her. After that, she wants the one above that.

description.value:
Trait

While Veronique holds a Crown & Cleaver proxy, the first time each round she would take damage, a bodyguard (use the thug or veteran stat block) within 30 feet can take the hit instead.

Trait

Veronique carries a Folio page. Once per day, when a creature she can see fails a Charisma saving throw, she can write a single sentence about them. It becomes true until the end of her next turn (it can't directly deal damage or kill).

Trait

If Veronique fails a saving throw, she can choose to succeed instead.

Actions

Veronique makes three Cleaver Rapier attacks, or two and uses Hostile Negotiation.

Actions

Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 14 (2d8 + 5) piercing damage plus 9 (2d8) necrotic damage.

Actions

One creature within 60 feet that can hear her makes a DC 19 Wisdom save [[/save wis dc=19]]. On a failure, the creature is charmed by her until the end of its next turn and must use its action to move away from her or to attack a creature she designates.

Actions

Veronique teleports to a Crown & Cleaver premises she has visited within 1 mile, along with anything she is carrying.

Reactions

When a creature within 30 feet targets her with an attack, Veronique imposes disadvantage on the roll by naming a price. If the attack still misses, the attacker has disadvantage on its next attack against her too.

items.name: Veronique is designed to be negotiated with, not fought

description.value:
Reactions

If the party has at least 2 Leverage against Crown & Cleaver, she never draws her blade on them first.

1bc5b3d48cb86e53.name: Veronique is designed to be negotiated with, not fought

biography.value: Every Gelatinous Cube franchise grows its desserts from a single primordial ooze kept frozen under the Sweet Covenant's refinery. It was old when the world was soft. It is awake, and it is hungry, and it has been franchised.

di.custom: blinded; charmed; deafened; exhaustion; frightened; prone

description.value:
Trait

The Mother Culture can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch wide without squeezing, and it occupies its entire space; other creatures can enter it (see Engulf).

Trait

Whenever the Mother Culture takes 30 or more damage from a single attack, a scoop (use the ochre jelly stat block) splits off in an unoccupied space within 10 feet.

Trait

Deep inside the Mother Culture, visible as a pale hard pearl, is the original drop. A creature engulfed by it can reach Sample Zero with a DC 20 Strength (Athletics) check. Removing Sample Zero ends the Culture's Regeneration permanently.

Trait

The Mother Culture regains 20 hit points at the start of its turn if it has at least 1 hit point and Sample Zero is still within it. Fire or cold damage of 20 or more in a round prevents this trait on its next turn.

Actions

The Mother Culture makes three Pseudopod attacks, and it can use Engulf.

Actions

Melee Weapon Attack: +13 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. Hit: 20 (3d8 + 7) bludgeoning damage plus 13 (3d8) acid damage.

Actions

The Mother Culture moves up to its speed. Each creature in its path makes a DC 21 Dexterity save [[/save dex dc=21]] or is engulfed, taking 35 (10d6) acid damage at the start of each of its turns. An engulfed creature is restrained and can't breathe; it can escape with a DC 21 Strength check.

Legendary Actions

The Mother Culture moves 10 feet.

Legendary Actions

Each engulfed creature takes 14 (4d6) acid damage.

Legendary Actions

Two scoops (ochre jellies) emerge and act immediately after the Culture.

biography.value: Every branch of the Golden Orcs stands beneath a pair of great golden tusks. Seen from above, they form the lines of one enormous seal—the Notarial Seal of Creation & Company. At each anchor branch, the tusks can stand up and walk.

languages.custom: understands the Notarial Oath but can't speak

description.value:
Trait

While the construct stands within 60 feet of its anchor branch, the Final Contract's Notarisation clause can't be voided, and the construct has advantage on saving throws.

Trait

The construct has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

Trait

The tusks shed bright light in a 60-foot radius. Creatures within it can't benefit from being invisible, and shadows there can't be used to hide.

Actions

The construct makes two Gore attacks.

Actions

Melee Weapon Attack: +14 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 30 (4d10 + 8) piercing damage. If the target is a creature, it makes a DC 22 Strength save [[/save str dc=22]] or is knocked prone.

Actions

The construct flares with golden light. Each creature within 30 feet makes a DC 20 Constitution save [[/save con dc=20]], taking 55 (10d10) radiant damage and becoming blinded until the end of its next turn on a failure, or half as much and not blinded on a success.

biography.value: Canonical identity: Mortimer Pell. Night manager of Wight Castle for 143 consecutive years; he wore the Murder King suit for twenty-two years. Someone killed him in it. The mascot now walks the dining room after closing, waving at nobody and trying to point at the door marked STAFF ONLY.

languages.custom: but only in the mascot's catchphrases

description.value:
Trait

Mortimer can only speak in Murder King slogans. Clever players can learn the truth by asking questions he can answer with one (Insight DC 12 [[/check skill=ins dc=12]] to interpret each).

Trait

If destroyed, Mortimer re-forms in the costume at the next closing time unless his killer is named aloud in the dining room.

Actions

Mortimer makes two Sceptre attacks.

Actions

Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) bludgeoning damage plus 3 (1d6) necrotic damage.

Actions

Each creature within 15 feet makes a DC 12 Wisdom save [[/save wis dc=12]] or is frightened until the end of its next turn. Children and the very drunk automatically succeed and wave back.

biography.value: Forty unseen servants, one voice, a picket sign held up by nothing. They want tea breaks, a name, and to be allowed to stop existing at the end of a shift rather than when a wizard forgets them.

languages.custom: Common (by moving objects to spell words)

description.value:
Trait

The swarm is invisible. Its sign is not.

Trait

The swarm can't be reduced below 1 hit point while at least one other unseen servant within 1 mile is on strike.

Actions

Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 0 ft., one creature in the swarm's space. Hit: 10 (4d4) bludgeoning damage, or 5 (2d4) if the swarm has half its hit points or fewer.

Actions

Every object within 30 feet that isn't being worn or carried floats 5 feet off the ground and stays there until the swarm's demands are heard.

biography.value: A small, precise man in a grey suit, with ink-stained fingers and a patient voice. He has owned himself for four hundred years. He is not cruel. He simply believes everything would work better if it belonged to someone, and that the someone should be him.

dr.custom: all damage while at least one clause of the final contract remains unvoided

languages.custom: every language that has a word for “sale”

description.value:
Trait

Tallis Vend can't die while Entry 1 of the Grand Ledger stands. When reduced to 0 hit points, he instead rewrites himself: he regains all his hit points and one unvoided clause of the Final Contract becomes permanently unvoidable except by the First Entry Receipt and a witness. If no clauses remain, he drops to 0 and the Ledger falls open to Entry 1.

Trait

Creatures that are signatories of any contract in the Grand Ledger deal half damage to Vend. A creature whose Contractor Agreement has been voided (Clause 77-B voided) ignores this trait.

items.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day, or 0 after the Minutes of Removal)

description.value:
Trait

If Vend fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed instead. If the party carries the Minutes of Removal (S23), he has no uses of this trait.

Trait

Until the Minutes of Removal are presented, each remaining Board director who hasn't flipped grants Vend +1 AC (to a maximum of +5).

Actions

Vend makes two Quill Strike attacks and uses Ledger Entry, or makes three Quill Strikes.

Actions

Melee or Ranged Spell Attack: +15 to hit, reach 10 ft. or range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 26 (4d8 + 8) force damage, and Vend learns one true fact about the target.

Actions

Vend writes one sentence in the Grand Ledger. Choose one: Repossession (one magic item a creature carries teleports to his hand; DC 23 Charisma save [[/save cha dc=23]] negates); Debit (one creature loses 40 hit points, no save, and can't regain them until it completes a long rest); Employ (two Compliance Officers appear within 30 feet); Amend (one voided clause is restored; a character holding its Receipt can make a DC 20 argument as a reaction to stop it).

Reactions

When a creature within 60 feet succeeds on a check to void a clause, Vend forces it to reroll. It must use the new roll. (Once per round.)

Legendary Actions

Vend regains 20 hit points.

Legendary Actions

One Compliance Officer within 60 feet makes a Stamp attack.

Legendary Actions

Vend uses Ledger Entry.

items.name: The fight is won with paper, not swords

description.value:
Legendary Actions

Each voided clause deals 35 psychic damage to Vend as reality stops agreeing with him. Voiding a clause is an action, even mid-combat.

Canonical identity: Hal Grundy. Membership Manager at the CostCo-op warehouse depot. He calls the extraordinary dragon board meeting, keeps a careful count of votes, and can still be persuaded by evidence that the membership system has hurt the people it claims to serve.
PT-07 — Murder King witness. Nervous employee with a notebook; a key witness to S2 and Mortimer Pell's death.
PT-11 — Room 303. Four legendary heroes asleep in dusty gear for decades. This sheet is a roleplay/group reference actor rather than a single combatant.
PT-18 — Lord Mayor of Brandmere. Chain of office, small ™ mark, and complete confidence that civic branding is governance.

S11 — The Beans of Pandemonium. A harvest worker who remembers the life she had before ABI's retention contract. She is practical, alert, and can lead the party through the wind-carved tunnels to the other workers.
Campaign guide NPC. Site foreman whose crew knows the dangerous shortcuts, shift changes, and maintenance routes. Treat him as a roleplay NPC unless the table makes the dispute violent.
Campaign guide NPC. A procedural-minded arbiter called when a contract dispute reaches formal review. The guide does not define a combat role.
S12 — All Rights Reserved. A cheerful druid at Goodberry's licensing booth who honestly believes spell licences are a sound wellness policy.
S12 — All Rights Reserved. Sister Wren's son. He survived the grey fever after his mother signed the licensing agreement that transferred ownership of Healing.

clones.name: Skarrow Vane
clones.description: S11 — The Beans of Pandemonium. ABI overseer and cambion on a performance bonus. Cruelty is how he hits his numbers; he may be bargained with if the party can make the incentives change.

clones.name: Collector Grix
clones.description: S13 — Pact of the Bucket. Accounts Receivable collector who arrives at midnight to collect the original franchise consideration: one soul.

clones.name: Clerk of the First Sale
clones.description: S14 — The Franchise Below. The ghostly clerk serving the first shop in history. Uses lich actions and spellcasting, weakened to 90 hp for this encounter.
